quote: A 2023 independent evaluation of CMMI models found that the vast majority had not achieved statistically significant reductions in Medicare spending or improvements in quality.
correct_fact: The 2023 independent assessment is CBO's Sept 2023 report: CMMI's activities increased net federal spending by $5.4B over 2011-2020 (0.1% of Medicare). GAO (2026): of 70 models tested by Jan 2025, four were expanded nationwide. 'Statistically significant ... quality' is not CBO's finding. 'Over fifteen years ... more than seventy models' (§3.2) is acceptable for 2026 (70 by Jan 2025 + LEAD, BALANCE etc.).
source_quote: increased net federal spending by $5.4 billion, or 0.1 percent of net spending on Medicare, between 2011 and 2020 / Of 70 models tested, the Innovation Center has expanded four models

quote: The models that showed the most promise --- ACO REACH (formerly Direct Contracting), AHEAD, the Making Care Primary model
correct_fact: AHEAD has no performance results (first PY 2026; Vermont withdrew) and the chapter itself says CMS ended MCP early on Dec 31, 2025. Cannot be 'showed the most promise'. Reframe as design characteristics.

quote: MSSP Track 1 (upside only for most participants)
correct_fact: Track 1 is the one-sided model by definition (42 CFR 425.604 'Calculation of savings under the one-sided model'); 'for most participants' is wrong for Track 1.
source_quote: § 425.604 Calculation of savings under the one-sided model.

quote: AHEAD ... five participants (Maryland, Connecticut, Hawaii, Rhode Island, and a downstate New York region) ... Vermont signed for Cohort 2 in January 2025 but withdrew in July 2026 ... ~$138M ... ~$10M cap
correct_fact: CONFIRMED: CMS AHEAD page lists Cohort 1 MD, Cohort 2 CT & HI, Cohort 3 RI & NY; NY DOH: five downstate counties; VTDigger 1/17/2025: Vermont enters second cohort; 30-day pre-launch / 6-month post-launch withdrawal notice (also confirms §3.5.1); Vermont withdrew July 2026. ACO REACH final PY 2026 and LEAD (voluntary, Jan 1 2027-2036) CONFIRMED. MCP (8 states, 2024, ended Dec 31 2025), BPCI-A end 12/31/2025, TEAM 2026-2030 CONFIRMED. ACO REACH 'equity focus including SDOH requirements' not checked against PY2026 changes (CMS PY2026 quick reference silent).
source_quote: Cohort 1: Maryland; Cohort 2: Connecticut and Hawaii; Cohort 3: Rhode Island and New York

quote: Medicaid launch May 2026; Medicare Part D launch postponed by CMS in April 2026, with a temporary Medicare GLP-1 Bridge demonstration in its place.
correct_fact: CMS April 21, 2026 memo delayed the Part D portion (planned Jan 2027); Medicaid states may begin any date between May 1, 2026 and Jan 1, 2027 (applications to July 31, 2026); Medicare GLP-1 Bridge launched July 1, 2026, extended through Dec 31, 2027. 'Medicaid launch May 2026' is only the earliest possible start.
source_quote: CMS ... is delaying implementation of the Medicare Part D portion of BALANCE for 2027

quote: SDOH investments --- since 2021, CMS has permitted states to use 1115 waiver funds for health-related social needs services, including housing supports, food assistance, and transportation
correct_fact: CMS's HRSN framework (Nov 2023 and Dec 2024 CIBs) was rescinded by a March 4, 2025 CMS bulletin; existing approved HRSN programs continue, new requests are considered case by case. The 2021 SDOH State Health Official letter was not rescinded.
source_quote: This policy change does not apply to existing HRSN programs ... CMS will consider states' applications ... on a case-by-case basis

quote: Vermont's recent 1115 amendment approval authorizes HRSN services --- enabling Blueprint's universal SDOH screening to connect to Medicaid-funded services
correct_fact: CMS's Jan 2, 2025 GC amendment authorizes HRSN HOUSING interventions (housing supports, medically necessary home remediation, accessibility modifications, short-term housing with clinical services; rent up to six months / medical respite for homeless enrollees) plus $10.9M infrastructure. 'Blueprint's universal SDOH screening' is not in the approval and 'universal' is unconfirmed.
source_quote: the state will receive authority to cover the following HRSN housing interventions: housing supports without room and board ...

quote: The current authorization runs through December 2027, with the AHEAD alignment provisions approved in a January 2025 amendment.
correct_fact: The Jan 2, 2025 amendment approved HRSN, SUD CIT, DD services and CRT/MH-under-22 transitions. It did NOT approve AHEAD-aligned provisions: CMS wrote that it and the state 'continue to collaborate on the state's request to institute a Medicaid global budget payment, consistent with ... AHEAD', with CMS TA 'through appropriate authorities, as identified by CMS'. Through Dec 31, 2027 CONFIRMED; originally approved 2005 CONFIRMED.
source_quote: CMS and the state continue to collaborate on the state's request to institute a Medicaid global budget payment, consistent with the requirements of the ... AHEAD Model.

quote: Vermont's Medicaid global budget shows the cost of skipping that negotiation
correct_fact: The state did not skip negotiation: the Jan 2025 approval letter records ongoing CMS-state collaboration on the Medicaid global budget. What happened is that it was implemented before CMS approval under the STCs (CMS July 7, 2026: not approved; not compliant with STCs 6.3(a), 6.4(i)(iii)).
source_quote: has not been approved by CMS in accordance with the requirements in Vermont's Global Commitment to Health ... STCs

quote: The administrative cost of prior authorization nationally is estimated in the tens of billions of dollars annually.
correct_fact: No source given and none confirmed. Delete. (13 hours/week incl. staff CONFIRMED: AMA 2024 survey, 39 PAs per physician per week.)
source_quote: practices complete 39 prior authorization requests per physician, per week ... 13 hours

quote: passed the House unanimously in 2022 ... 2024 rules require payers to respond to expedited PA requests within 72 hours and standard PA requests within 7 days
correct_fact: H.R. 3173 passed the House by voice vote (Sept 14, 2022), not a recorded unanimous vote. CMS-0057-F (Jan 2024) is one rule and applies to Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, CHIP and federally-facilitated-exchange QHP issuers (from Jan 1, 2026), not all payers.

quote: Vermont's Health Care Advocate has documented PA denial rates and challenged insurance rate filings that include excessive PA complexity costs.
correct_fact: No source found for either claim. Delete. (Act 167 Sec. 11 description of DFR/GMCB prior-authorization work CONFIRMED.)
source_quote: The Department of Financial Regulation shall direct health insurers to provide prior authorization information to the Department ...

quote: providers described the CON process and prior authorization as major barriers to efficient care delivery, with cost-effective contracts unable to be secured in time due to administrative friction
correct_fact: Oliver Wyman's system map ties 'Cost-effective contracts cannot be secured due to long approval process' to the CON/licensure approval process, not to prior authorization; prior authorization appears in its recommendations ('Further simplify prior authorization, CON process and Medicaid billing'; 'simplify prior authorization process and state agency documentation').
source_quote: Cost-effective contracts cannot be secured due to long approval process

quote: Act 68 RBP compliance planning for FY2027 ... assess AHEAD primary care participation options
correct_fact: GMCB sets the RBP rule in 2027; maximum rates take effect HFY2028. Vermont withdrew from AHEAD in July 2026, so AHEAD participation is no longer an option for Vermont organizations. Act 68 $2M transformation grants CONFIRMED.

quote: $911 billion in Medicaid cuts over 10 years --- the largest reduction in federal health spending in American history.
correct_fact: $911B (CBO, federal Medicaid, 10 yrs), 10 million uninsured by 2034, $137B rural (KFF) CONFIRMED. The 'largest ... in American history' superlative is advocacy framing with no authoritative source located; delete.
source_quote: CBO estimates the enacted package would cut federal Medicaid spending by $911 billion over ten years

quote: Eligibility redetermination every 6 months instead of annually
correct_fact: Six-month redeterminations apply to expansion adults only (DVHA: first check at 2027 renewal, then every 6 months).
source_quote: you will have to renew your Medicaid every 6 months

quote: Provider tax restrictions: ban on new or higher provider taxes in expansion states; phase-down of existing taxes / In effect for new taxes; phase-down beginning 2027 / modeling through 2031
correct_fact: H.R. 1 bars new or increased provider taxes in ALL states; the safe-harbor phase-down (6% to 3.5%, 0.5 pt/yr) applies to expansion states starting FY2028 (Oct 1, 2027) and reaches 3.5% in FY2032.
source_quote: H.R.1 prohibits states from creating new provider taxes or raising taxable rates ... drops by 0.5 points a year starting in FY2028 (October 1, 2027) until ... 3.5% in FY 2032

quote: State-directed payment caps at 100% of Medicare (expansion states) | 2027 | ... Vermont hospitals receiving state-directed supplemental payments face revenue reduction
correct_fact: New SDPs are capped at 100% (expansion) / 110% of Medicare on enactment; grandfathered SDPs step down 10 pts/yr starting Jan 2028. MANUAL: the 'When' cell reads just '2027' (single-token paragraph, not pair-able safely) - change it to 'New payments on enactment; existing payments from 2028'. Whether any Vermont hospital receives SDPs is unconfirmed (Vermont Medicaid is not conventional risk-based managed care); pair softens with 'any'.
source_quote: For existing (grandfathered) SDPs, the ceiling falls 10 percentage points per year ... starting January 2028

quote: Medicaid reimbursement reductions (DSH cuts, payment rate changes)
correct_fact: DSH cuts are ACA-scheduled reductions, not an H.R. 1 provision; the $911B/$137B is the law's combined effect. Relabel the row.

quote: Sources: KFF analysis; CBO estimates; Pew Charitable Trusts (January 2026).
correct_fact: No Pew January 2026 item identified as a basis for any figure in the table; figures trace to CBO/KFF and Georgetown CCF. Replace Pew with Georgetown CCF (already in chapter Sources). Count 2 (caption + Figure Index).

quote: Vermont's hospitals were already projecting 5-year cumulative deficits of $700 million to $2.4 billion
correct_fact: The projection is Oliver Wyman's (Act 167 report), not the hospitals' own.

quote: Mandatory for Vermont's expansion adults (ages 19--64) from January 1, 2027; DVHA has begun notifying members.
correct_fact: CONFIRMED: DVHA contacting members from August 2026; requirements start Jan 1, 2027 for some adults 19-64; 80 hours/month.
source_quote: The agency will start communicating ... with other members in August 2026

quote: Final rules typically take effect 60 days after publication, but proposed rules give 60-90 days of advance notice
correct_fact: APA: final rules generally effective no sooner than 30 days after publication; major rules 60 days (Congressional Review Act). Comment periods are typically 30-60 days (CMS payment rules usually 60). '60-90 days' overstated.

quote: The Policy Strategy service line uses a four-phase engagement structure
correct_fact: Ch12 §12.3.1 describes the Policy Strategy service line as a THREE-phase structure. The four items here are the Policy Impact Assessment Framework's steps (the tool at /research-lab/policy-quality?tab=policy-impact implements exactly these four steps). Also: the 'Stakeholder communication' item is not bulleted like the other three (format check).
source_quote: The typical engagement follows a three-phase structure

quote: §3.8 platform table and Academy line
correct_fact: CONFIRMED: Work Requirements Calculator (exemption-rate and admin-error-rate inputs deliver 'nominal exemptions vs. administrative churn'), H.R. 1 Cliff Scenario, Medicaid Eligibility Simulator routes and tools.ts entries tag ch3; Track 2 lesson 'CMMI Models, Waivers, and the Federal–State Interface'; Medicaid 101 track 'Waivers & State Flexibility'; medicare-fundamentals published (Supabase). Gap, not a defect: the Policy Impact Assessment Framework the chapter defines in §3.7.2 (tool tags ch3) is not in the §3.8 table.

quote: your organization will be operating under prospective hospital global budgets beginning in hospital FY2028
correct_fact: Act 68: one or more non-CAH hospitals from HFY2028, all hospitals by HFY2030, both 'to the extent resources are available'. (The risk-adjustment sentence has already been corrected in the docx by the editor: 'Act 68 does not specify a risk adjustment method...'.)
source_quote: Beginning not later than hospital fiscal year 2028, to the extent that resources are available ... one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals

quote: especially the analytics tools and the HSA Coordinator positions --- before performance accountability begins. Appropriating for these positions is not optional; it is the enabling condition for the federal investment Vermont has committed to.
correct_fact: HSA Coordinator positions are the BOOK'S OWN PROPOSAL (Ch16 roadmap), not an existing AHS program; the Act 119 report kept AHS unified. 'The federal investment Vermont has committed to' is stale: Vermont withdrew from AHEAD (July 2026) and the Medicaid global budget was halted; Act 68 global budgets are state-authority.

quote: AHEAD's predecessor --- the Vermont All-Payer ACO Model, and its ACO, OneCare Vermont --- failed partly because organizations assumed financial risk without the analytics to manage it.
correct_fact: Causal claim is the book's own thesis (Ch1 OneCare autopsy), consistent with the front matter; not independently sourced. Left as-is.
